note: **Visible in some translations and not in others, which is the reason to note it.** KJV has the good shepherd 'lays down His life for the sheep' (John 10:11) and the greater love 'lay down his life for his friends' (John 15:13) -- two different verbs, no verbal link. Every other translation the graph carries -- ASV, WEB, BSB and YLT -- renders John 10:11 as laying down his life. The KJV is the only one of the five that does not, which makes it the same phrase as John 15:13 and 1John 3:16. A reader in the KJV cannot see the join; a reader in a modern translation cannot miss it. The edge is held because the join is in the corpus, and marked implied because the KJV wording does not carry it.

'that he lay down his life for his friends' (John 15:13); 'Jesus laid down His life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers' (1John 3:16). The phrase is the same in both and the letter turns the measure into an obligation. Neither text cites the other, so the pairing is the graph's; the wording is the corpus's.
'Greater love has no one than this' (John 15:13).

Laying a life down, and losing it to save it. Both are about a life given up rather than kept, and both make the giving up the point. The corpus does not connect them and the vocabulary differs -- lay down against lose -- so this is the graph's pairing on the shape rather than on the words.
'By this we know what love is: Jesus laid down His life for us' (1John 3:16).
